What now works: every canon audit report carries a subresource-reach axis, and the intermittent calibration failure is attributable to a named resource.

```
reached: status=[200] examined=[...] subresourceFail=["1440px:0","1024px:0","768px:0","375px:0"] ...
console: 1440px Failed to load resource: … 404 () <- https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/archivo/v25/….woff2
```

What I measured (6 independent full runs, 22 tests each):

| | result | what varied |
|---|---|---|
| before (3 runs) | 3/3 green | **nothing** — all 19 audit outputs identical on status, examined, canon |
| after (3 runs) | 1 green / 2 red | file and width only: `screen-06@1440px`, `light-01@768px` |

Both reds were the same cause: a **404 on the remote Archivo woff2 from `fonts.gstatic.com`**. The prototypes are `file://` but pull remote fonts, so a transient CDN 404 becomes a console error, and a console error is one of `hardFailCount()`'s five terms. Why the 404 happens (rate limit vs. transient CDN) is marked `[확인 필요]` in the code — out of scope here.

One thing the instrumentation exposed that I did not expect: `subresourceFail=2` while `console=1`. The console axis **undercounts** subresource failures. Mechanism marked `[확인 필요]`; likely relevant to step 2.

Unchanged as required: `hardFailCount()`, `CANON_BASELINE`/`LIGHT_BASELINE`, and `design-canon-calibration.spec.ts` (AC-3 rc=0). Diff is one file.
